title: Molten Aluminum-Induced Corrosion and Wear-Resistance Properties of ZrB<sub>2</sub>-Based Cermets Improved by Sintering-Temperature Manipulation.

recollection.starting_material: ZrB2 powders with a metallic binder phase (e.g., Ni or Co)
recollection.intervention: Systematic variation of sintering temperature (likely spark plasma sintering between ~1600 °C and 1800 °C)
recollection.structure: Densified ZrB2-based cermet with a fine, well-bonded ceramic-grain and binder-phase microstructure, possibly with in situ-formed ZrC or boride second phases
recollection.mechanism: Higher sintering temperature enhances densification and binder wetting, reduces porosity, and promotes interfacial reactions that seal grain boundaries against molten Al penetration
recollection.results: At the optimal sintering temperature (around 1700 °C), the cermet reached ~98 % theoretical density, showed molten-Al corrosion rates below ~0.02 mg/cm2·h at 750 °C, and exhibited a wear rate of ~1×10−6 mm3/(N·m) under sliding against hardened steel

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies spark plasma sintering-temperature variation, but gives the wrong temperature range and optimum (actual: 1300–1600 °C, optimum 1500 °C). Its dense, well-bonded microstructure description is directionally correct, though the suggested ZrC/boride phases are unsupported and it misses binder overflow and porosity at 1600 °C. The proposed densification, binder-wetting, pore-reduction, and suppressed Al-penetration mechanism is substantially correct, but omits deterioration from binder loss above the optimum. Quantitatively, ~98% density is close to 97.71%, while the optimum temperature, corrosion metric/value, and wear metric/value are incorrect.
